t: A Muslim sultanate at the northern tip of Sumatra that rose after the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511 and dominated the pepper trade.
Under Iskandar Muda (1607–1636) it conquered much of Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula but lost its fleet at Malacca in 1629.
Its scholars made it a centre of Malay Islam, and it fought the Dutch from 1873 until the sultan surrendered in 1903.
dyk: Four queens ruled Aceh in succession from 1641 to 1699, beginning with Taj ul-Alam Safiatuddin Syah, daughter of the conqueror Iskandar Muda.
ev: Ali Mughayat Syah conquers Pasai and drives out the Portuguese
Alauddin al-Kahhar besieges Malacca after seeking Ottoman military aid
Iskandar Muda sacks Batu Sawar, the capital of Johor
Aceh's armada is destroyed at Malacca by the Portuguese and their allies
Taj ul-Alam Safiatuddin becomes the first of four ruling queens
The Netherlands declares war, beginning the Aceh War
A Dutch expedition captures the sultan's palace
Sultan Muhammad Daud Syah surrenders to the Dutch

f.capital: Bandar Aceh Darussalam (later Kutaraja, now Banda Aceh)
